correctness.rationale: Uniform radial Hessian bounds imply strong concavity of the exact moment-density log function and unique saddle r_n phi'(r_n)=n+d-1/2. Gaussian upper tails and a local lower normalizer give a dimension-independent-in-n relative O(n^-1/2) eigenvalue estimate. Monotone likelihood-ratio ordering proves eigenvalues are decreasing and assures counting all homogeneous degrees. The binomial multiplicity gives the singular-value profile; threshold bracketing within a fixed radius yields n_t=q(R_t)+O(R_t) and the O(t^(1/beta)) normalized counting formula. Continuity and dense saddle sampling prove the full interval and necessary-and-sufficient criterion. Both explicit examples were differentiated to verify Hessian bounds. 162 finite diagnostics passed; analytic reasoning, not finite checks, establishes the theorem.

Exact phase-space density and the multiplicity factor are natural spectral invariants, not arbitrarily selected numerical slices.
